question: Comment l'AI Act traite-t-il un produit d'IA civil réutilisé ensuite à des fins militaires ou de sécurité nationale ?
ground_truth: An AI system placed on the market for civilian or law enforcement purposes that is used, with or without modification, for military, defence or national security purposes does not fall within the scope of the AI Act, whatever the type of entity carrying out those activities. The use of AI systems for national security, military and defence purposes is excluded from the scope of the Regulation.

key_facts.fact: outside the scope of the Regulation
regardless of the type of entity

notes: P44: the 7b draft said 'can use' (scope exclusion turned into a permission). rewrite proposed by Claude (5.4-B) - HIGH-RISK verified line by line by Chloe (2026-10-18, side-by-side aid prepared by Claude): matches source

question: Que doit contenir la demande qu'un fournisseur adresse à un organisme notifié pour l'évaluation de la documentation technique de son système d'IA à haut risque, selon l'AI Act ?
ground_truth: The application must include the name and address of the provider, a written declaration that the same application has not been lodged with any other notified body, and the technical documentation referred to in Annex IV.

key_facts.fact: not lodged with any other notified body

notes: rewrite proposed by Claude (5.4-B) - spot-check only (not verified line by line)

question: Quand un déployeur enregistre un système d'IA à haut risque dans la base de données de l'UE, quelles informations l'AI Act lui impose-t-il de fournir ?
ground_truth: Deployers registering a high-risk AI system under Article 49(3) must provide, and keep up to date, their name, address and contact details; those of the person submitting the information on their behalf; the URL of the provider's entry for the AI system in the EU database; a summary of the findings of the fundamental rights impact assessment carried out under Article 27; and, where applicable, a summary of the data protection impact assessment.

key_facts.fact: summary of the fundamental rights impact assessment
URL of the provider's entry in the EU database

notes: rewrite proposed by Claude (5.4-B) - spot-check only (not verified line by line)

question: How does the AI Act define an 'AI system'?
ground_truth: An AI system is a machine-based system designed to operate with varying levels of autonomy, that may exhibit adaptiveness after deployment, and that, for explicit or implicit objectives, infers from the input it receives how to generate outputs such as predictions, content, recommendations or decisions that can influence physical or virtual environments.
notes: Article 3(1); not the smoke question (Q5 is Article 6). rewrite proposed by Claude (5.4-B) - spot-check only (not verified line by line)

question: Selon l'AI Act, que doit faire le fournisseur d'un outil d'IA générative pour que les images, sons ou textes qu'il produit puissent être reconnus comme générés par une IA ?

markers: Article 50 Obligations de transparence pour les fournisseurs et les déployeurs de certains systèmes d’IA
Article 50 Transparency obligations for providers and deployers of certain AI systems

ground_truth: Les fournisseurs de systèmes d'IA, y compris de systèmes d'IA à usage général, qui génèrent des contenus de synthèse de type audio, image, vidéo ou texte veillent à ce que les sorties soient marquées dans un format lisible par machine et identifiables comme ayant été générées ou manipulées par une IA. Cette obligation ne s'applique pas lorsque le système remplit une fonction d'assistance pour la mise en forme standard ou ne modifie pas de manière substantielle les données d'entrée, ni lorsque l'utilisation est autorisée par la loi à des fins de prévention ou de détection des infractions pénales.

key_facts.fact: générées ou manipulées par une IA

notes: Article 50(2); the ground truth keeps the two exceptions. rewrite proposed by Claude (5.4-B) - HIGH-RISK verified line by line by Chloe (2026-10-18, side-by-side aid prepared by Claude): matches source

question: Under the CRR, what share of the assets behind French FCT senior units used as covered-bond collateral must be residential mortgages?

markers: Article 129 Exposures in the form of covered bonds

ground_truth: The assets underlying such senior units must, at any time while they are in the cover pool, be at least 90 % composed of residential mortgages combined with any prior liens up to the lesser of the principal amounts due under the units, the principal amounts of the liens, and 80 % of the value of the pledged properties. The units must also qualify for credit quality step 1 and must not exceed 10 % of the nominal amount of the outstanding issue.

key_facts.fact: not more than 10 % of the outstanding issue

notes: Wording of the CRR version in the corpus (FCT units; later amended by the covered bond package - not in the corpus). rewrite proposed by Claude (5.4-B) - HIGH-RISK verified line by line by Chloe (2026-10-18, side-by-side aid prepared by Claude): matches source

question: What does the CRR require a bank to do to be sure its financial collateral can actually be enforced?
ground_truth: Institutions must fulfil any contractual and statutory requirements and take all steps necessary to ensure the enforceability of the collateral arrangements under the law applicable to their interest in the collateral. They must have conducted sufficient legal review confirming enforceability in all relevant jurisdictions, and re-conduct that review as necessary to ensure continuing enforceability.
notes: rewrite proposed by Claude (5.4-B) - spot-check only (not verified line by line)

question: Under the CRR, which kind of clause prevents a netting agreement from being recognised?

markers: Article 296 Recognition of contractual netting agreements

ground_truth: A contractual netting agreement is recognised only if, among other conditions, the contract contains no clause which, in the event of a counterparty's default, permits the non-defaulting counterparty to make only limited payments, or no payments at all, to the estate of the defaulting party, even if the defaulting party is a net creditor (a 'walk away clause').

key_facts.fact: limited payments or no payments at all

notes: rewrite proposed by Claude (5.4-B) - spot-check only (not verified line by line)

question: Under the CRR large exposure rules, what extra own funds charge applies when a trading book exposure has exceeded the limit for no more than 10 days?

markers: Article 397 Calculating additional own funds requirements for large exposures in the trading book

ground_truth: Where the excess has not persisted for more than 10 days, the additional own funds requirement is 200 % of the requirements on the components selected under paragraph 1 (the components of the trading exposure that attract the highest specific-risk requirements). From 10 days after the excess, the components are allocated to Table 1 and multiplied by factors from 200 % up to 900 % depending on the size of the excess.
notes: Article 397; not the smoke question (Q4 is Article 395). rewrite proposed by Claude (5.4-B) - HIGH-RISK verified line by line by Chloe (2026-10-18, side-by-side aid prepared by Claude): matches source

question: Which kinds of financial firms does DORA leave out because they are already exempt or only lightly regulated under their sector rules?
ground_truth: Les gestionnaires de fonds d'investissement alternatifs visés à l'article 3, paragraphe 2, de la directive 2011/61/UE, les entreprises d'assurance et de réassurance visées à l'article 4 de la directive 2009/138/CE et les institutions de retraite professionnelle gérant des régimes de retraite qui, ensemble, n'ont pas plus de quinze affiliés au total ne sont pas incluses dans le champ d'application de DORA, car ce ne serait pas proportionné. Les intermédiaires d'assurance, de réassurance et à titre accessoire qui sont des microentreprises ou des PME ne devraient pas non plus relever du règlement.
notes: rewrite proposed by Claude (5.4-B) - HIGH-RISK verified line by line by Chloe (2026-10-18, side-by-side aid prepared by Claude): matches source

question: Selon DORA, quels droits une banque doit-elle conserver dans son contrat avec un prestataire TIC qui soutient des fonctions critiques ou importantes ?
ground_truth: Les contrats de fourniture de services TIC qui soutiennent des fonctions critiques ou importantes devraient permettre l'exercice des droits d'accès, d'inspection et d'audit par l'entité financière ou par un tiers désigné, ainsi que le droit de prendre des copies, pour assurer un suivi permanent des performances du prestataire. L'autorité compétente de l'entité financière devrait aussi pouvoir, moyennant préavis, inspecter et auditer le prestataire tiers de services TIC.
notes: rewrite proposed by Claude (5.4-B) - spot-check only (not verified line by line)

question: Selon DORA, quelles conditions supplémentaires s'appliquent lorsqu'une entité financière veut confier ses tests de pénétration fondés sur la menace à ses propres testeurs internes ?

markers: Article 27 Exigences applicables aux testeurs afin de réaliser des tests de pénétration fondés sur la menace

ground_truth: En plus des exigences applicables à tous les testeurs (paragraphe 1), le recours aux testeurs internes doit avoir été approuvé par l'autorité compétente concernée ou par l'autorité publique unique désignée ; l'autorité compétente doit avoir vérifié que l'entité financière dispose de ressources suffisantes et veillé à éviter les conflits d'intérêts pendant la conception et l'exécution du test ; et le fournisseur de renseignements sur les menaces doit être externe à l'entité financière.

key_facts.fact: fournisseur de renseignements sur les menaces externe

notes: Article 27(2). rewrite proposed by Claude (5.4-B) - spot-check only (not verified line by line)

question: According to the ACPR's 2020 discussion paper on AI governance, how did bringing machine learning into credit-scoring models change governance?

sections: Juin 2020 Gouvernance des algorithmes d’intelligence artificielle dans le secteur financier Document de réflexion AUTEURS Laurent Dupont, Olivier Fliche, Su Yang Pôle Fintech-Innovation, ACPR > 2.2. Travaux exploratoires > 2.2.2. Thème 2 : Modèles internes en banque et assurance

ground_truth: Les deux scénarios étudiés (un grand groupe bancaire et un cabinet de conseil) ont montré trois impacts de gouvernance : une technicité accrue du processus de validation initiale, la mise en place d'outils de monitoring pour le contrôle interne, et l'intégration de méthodes explicatives afin d'assurer le contrôle permanent ainsi que les missions d'audit.
notes: rewrite proposed by Claude (5.4-B) - spot-check only (not verified line by line)

question: Selon le document de l'ACPR de 2020 sur la gouvernance de l'IA, où les superviseurs pourraient-ils être formés à la data science ?

sections: Juin 2020 Gouvernance des algorithmes d’intelligence artificielle dans le secteur financier Document de réflexion AUTEURS Laurent Dupont, Olivier Fliche, Su Yang Pôle Fintech-Innovation, ACPR > ÉVALUATION EMPIRIQUE DU ML > 5.5.2. Enjeux spécifiques aux superviseurs

ground_truth: Pour accompagner l'adaptation des méthodes, outils et données du superviseur, le document évoque une formation en Data Science soit chez le superviseur – ce qui est envisagé au sein de l'ACPR –, soit dans des instituts spécialisés (par exemple dans le domaine de la conformité en banque ou de l'actuariat).
notes: 7b draft was a yes/no question. rewrite proposed by Claude (5.4-B) - spot-check only (not verified line by line)

question: Dans l'atelier LCB-FT décrit par l'ACPR, à quelle condition le modèle de ML de la banque génère-t-il une alerte pour une transaction ayant un score élevé ?
ground_truth: Dans l'atelier complémentaire LCB-FT, un filtre fait qu'une transaction ayant obtenu un score élevé par le modèle de ML ne génère une alerte que si aucune alerte n'a été levée par le moteur de règles métier sur ce même client dans les trois mois précédents. Ces alertes supplémentaires sont envoyées directement au niveau N2.

key_facts.fact: aucune alerte du moteur de règles métier

notes: rewrite proposed by Claude (5.4-B) - spot-check only (not verified line by line)

question: Comment le document de réflexion de l'ACPR de 2020 classe-t-il les méthodes d'explicabilité en machine learning ?

sections: Annexes > 11. Recension des méthodes explicatives en IA

ground_truth: Les méthodes d'explication se répartissent en trois catégories selon la phase de conception et d'utilisation du modèle : les méthodes pré-modélisation, qui visent à comprendre et décrire les données utilisées ; les méthodes conjointes à la modélisation, qui contribuent à concevoir des modèles intrinsèquement plus explicables ; et les méthodes post-modélisation, qui produisent des explications à partir de modèles déjà conçus et entraînés.
notes: rewrite proposed by Claude (5.4-B) - spot-check only (not verified line by line)

question: Selon les orientations de l'ABE sur l'externalisation, dans quels cas une banque doit-elle toujours considérer une fonction externalisée comme critique ou importante ?

sections: 4. Guidelines on outsourcing > Title II – Assessment of outsourcing arrangements > 4 Critical or important functions

ground_truth: Institutions and payment institutions should always consider a function as critical or important (a) where a defect or failure in its performance would materially impair their continuing compliance with their authorisation conditions or regulatory obligations, their financial performance, or the soundness or continuity of their banking and payment services; (b) when operational tasks of internal control functions are outsourced, unless the assessment shows that a failure would not adversely affect the effectiveness of the internal control function; and (c) when they intend to outsource banking or payment activities to an extent that would require authorisation by a competent authority.
notes: Paragraph 29 of the guidelines: numbered paragraphs can trigger P38 (paragraph number cited as a passage number). The 7b ground truth merged paragraphs 29 and 31. rewrite proposed by Claude (5.4-B) - HIGH-RISK verified line by line by Chloe (2026-10-18, side-by-side aid prepared by Claude): matches source

question: When outsourcing, what must a bank do so that it does not become an 'empty shell', according to the EBA outsourcing guidelines?

sections: 4. Guidelines on outsourcing > Title III – Governance framework > 6 Sound governance arrangements and outsourcing

ground_truth: Institutions and payment institutions should maintain sufficient substance at all times and not become 'empty shells' or 'letter-box entities'. To this end they should meet all the conditions of their authorisation at all times, retain a clear and transparent organisational framework and structure that ensures compliance with legal and regulatory requirements, exercise appropriate oversight and manage the risks where operational tasks of internal control functions are outsourced, and have sufficient resources and capacities to do so.

key_facts.fact: not become empty shells or letter-box entities

notes: Paragraph 39 (the source chunk also holds 38-40). rewrite proposed by Claude (5.4-B) - spot-check only (not verified line by line)

question: What mapping exercise do the EBA ICT and security risk guidelines expect from financial institutions?

sections: Guidelines on ICT and security risk management > 3.3. ICT and security risk management framework > 3.3.2. Identification of functions, processes and assets

ground_truth: Financial institutions should identify, establish and keep updated a mapping of their business functions, roles and supporting processes, to identify the importance of each and their interdependencies related to ICT and security risks. They should also keep an updated mapping of the information assets supporting those functions and processes, such as ICT systems, staff, contractors, third parties and dependencies on other internal and external systems and processes, so as to manage at least the assets that support their critical business functions.
notes: rewrite proposed by Claude (5.4-B) - spot-check only (not verified line by line)

question: Dans les orientations de l'ABE sur les risques liés aux TIC et à la sécurité, que signifient RTO et RPO pour les plans de continuité d'activité ?

sections: Guidelines on ICT and security risk management > 3.7. Business continuity management > 3.7.2. Business continuity planning

ground_truth: Business continuity plans should allow financial institutions to recover the operations of their critical business activities after disruptions within a recovery time objective (RTO), the maximum time within which a system or process must be restored after an incident, and a recovery point objective (RPO), the maximum time period during which it is acceptable for data to be lost in the event of an incident.
notes: rewrite proposed by Claude (5.4-B) - spot-check only (not verified line by line)

question: Under the EBA loan origination guidelines, how should a bank handle a third-party guarantee on a loan to a company?

sections: 5. Loan origination procedures > 5.2 Assessment of borrower’s creditworthiness > 5.2.6 Lending to medium-sized and large enterprises

ground_truth: If a loan agreement involves any form of guarantee from third parties, institutions should assess the level of protection provided by the guarantee and, if relevant, carry out a creditworthiness assessment of the guarantor, applying the relevant provisions of the guidelines depending on whether the guarantor is a natural person or an enterprise. This assessment should be proportionate to the size of the guarantee relative to the loan and to the type of guarantor.

key_facts.fact: proportionate to the size of the guarantee

notes: rewrite proposed by Claude (5.4-B) - spot-check only (not verified line by line)

question: According to the EBA loan origination guidelines, what is a 'hung transaction' in leveraged lending?

sections: 8. Monitoring framework > 8.2 Monitoring of credit exposures and borrowers

ground_truth: Institutions engaged in syndicating leveraged transactions should identify failed syndications, i.e. transactions that were not syndicated within 90 days following the commitment date. They should set up a dedicated framework to deal with these 'hung transactions' covering holding strategy, booking and accounting practices, regulatory classification and the subsequent capital requirements calculation.
notes: rewrite proposed by Claude (5.4-B) - spot-check only (not verified line by line)

question: Under the EBA internal governance guidelines, which banks have to set up risk, nomination and remuneration committees?
ground_truth: All institutions that are themselves significant, considering the individual, sub- consolidated and consolidated levels, must establish risk, nomination and remuneration committees to advise the management body in its supervisory function and prepare its decisions. Non-significant institutions, including those within the scope of prudential consolidation of a significant institution, are not obliged to establish those committees.
notes: rewrite proposed by Claude (5.4-B) - HIGH-RISK verified line by line by Chloe (2026-10-18, side-by-side aid prepared by Claude): matches source

question: Under the EBA internal governance guidelines, what extra information must a bank be able to give its supervisor about a large loan to a board member?

sections: 4. Guidelines > 12.2 Documentation of loans to members of the management body and their related parties and additional information

ground_truth: For a loan to a member of the management body or their related parties above EUR 200 000, institutions should be able to provide to the competent authority on request: the percentage of the loan, and of all outstanding loans to the same debtor, compared with the sum of Tier 1 and Tier 2 capital and with common equity Tier 1 capital; whether the loan is part of a large exposure; and the relative weight of all outstanding loans to that debtor as a percentage of all outstanding loans to members of the management body and their related parties.

key_facts.fact: whether part of a large exposure

notes: P47: the 7b draft wrote 'EUR 200,000'; the source writes 'EUR 200 000'. rewrite proposed by Claude (5.4-B) - HIGH-RISK verified line by line by Chloe (2026-10-18, side-by-side aid prepared by Claude): matches source

question: According to the EBA report on machine learning for IRB models, how does the April 2023 text of the proposed Consumer Credit Directive restrict the data used for creditworthiness assessment?

sections: 5. Interaction with (non-CRR) regulatory frameworks > 5.1 Interaction with GDPR

ground_truth: The April 2023 text of the proposed CCD refers to personal data under Article 9 of the GDPR when prohibiting the use of specific personal data for creditworthiness assessment, also where the data were received from databases located in other Member States. It also prohibits the use of data collected from social networks and refers to the GDPR data minimisation principle in its requirements for assessing consumers' creditworthiness.
notes: rewrite proposed by Claude (5.4-B) - spot-check only (not verified line by line)

question: Que recommande l'ABE d'éviter pour que les modèles NI fondés sur le machine learning ne deviennent pas inutilement complexes ?

sections: Annex I– Principle-based recommendations Recommendations regarding the regulatory compliant use of ML techniques in the context of the IRB framework

ground_truth: Institutions are recommended to balance model performance and explainability and to avoid unnecessary complexity that is not justified by a significant improvement in predictive capacity. In particular they should avoid including an excessive number of explanatory drivers or drivers with no significant predictive information, using unstructured data when more conventional data with similar predictive capacity is available, and overly complex modelling choices when simpler approaches give similar results.
notes: rewrite proposed by Claude (5.4-B) - spot-check only (not verified line by line)
